column4: Visit note | 2025-10-28 10:00 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Afsana Begum, 73, female. Mrs. Begum reports stiffness in her knees for a few minutes in the morning and pain when using the stairs. She mentions her discomfort has been worse since standing all day at a shop in Narayanganj. She works as a madrasa teacher, lives at home with her family, and denies any history of trauma. She has no known comorbidities. She reports no joint swelling, locking, or sudden giving way. On examination: BMI 33.1, BP 118/74 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 78 kg. Knee range of motion is slightly restricted with mild crepitus, but no effusion. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-11-01 04:00 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Saad Munshi, 26, male. Mr. Munshi describes feeling tense with tight muscles and constant worry for months. He notes these feelings have become worse since a family business loss in Sirajganj. He works as a call centre agent and lives with roommates. He has a history of Hypothyroidism. He denies any panic attacks, suicidal ideation, or substance use. On examination: GAD-7 score 18, BP 128/70 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 82 kg. He is alert and oriented, with anxious affect but normal speech and thought flow. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-11-03 09:30 AM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Habib Rahman, 74, male. Mr. Rahman states he experiences pain on stairs, a creaking sensation in his knee, and morning stiffness lasting a few minutes. He notes his symptoms became worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Jashore. He is a retired civil servant, lives with his spouse, and has a background of Bronchial asthma. He denies any recent falls, severe locking, or night pain. On examination: BMI 30.7, BP 121/83 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 86 kg. Joint examination reveals crepitus on movement without acute inflammation or warmth. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-11-03 10:30 AM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Laila Sultana, 58, female. Mrs. Sultana presents complaining of a creaking knee and brief morning stiffness lasting a few minutes. She mentions the trouble has been worse since standing all day at a shop in Narayanganj. She works as a sales representative, lives with her family, and has no comorbidity. She denies any sharp locking or major instability. On examination: BMI 31.5, BP 119/81 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 57 kg. Knee flexion is mildly uncomfortable with palpable crepitus, and peripheral pulses are intact. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-11-04 11:30 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Shirin Howlader, 57, female. Mrs. Howlader reports looking pale and getting breathless on the stairs. She notes this was noticed after months of skipping lunch during long shifts in Rangpur. She works as a schoolteacher, lives with her children, and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any chest pain, dizziness, or gastrointestinal bleeding. On examination: haemoglobin 8.8 g/dL, BP 130/85 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 69 kg. Conjunctivae are pale, and heart sounds are normal without murmurs. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. Tests ordered before starting treatment: a complete blood count and serum ferritin. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-11-05 11:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Mamun Majumder, 24, male. Mr. Majumder complains of pimples and blackheads on his face along with marks left behind after the pimples. He states it has been worse since working in a hot kitchen in Tangail. He works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver, lives with relatives, and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any significant pain or systemic fever. On examination: about 10 inflamed spots on the face, BP 113/72 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, weight 81 kg. Skin shows papules and comedones without deep scarring or cysts. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. Tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and avoid squeezing spots. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-11-05 12:00 PM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Tania Miah, 68, female. Mrs. Miah expresses deep worry about her sleep and waking up tired every morning. She states her troubles began after a newborn arrived in the family in Cox's Bazar. She is a homemaker, lives with extended family, and has no other medical conditions. She denies daytime hallucinations, severe mood swings, or neurological deficits. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 17, BP 134/70 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 67 kg. She appears fatigued but is cooperative and coherent throughout the conversation. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. Referral to Neurology in this clinic for further assessment. She was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up after the Neurology review.

Visit note | 2025-11-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Lubna Rahman, Endocrinology | Patient: Liton Molla, 59, male. Mr. Molla describes feeling low on energy after working indoors all day. He mentions his fatigue started after staying indoors during a long illness in Farmgate. He works as a police constable, lives alone, and has no comorbidity. He denies bone pain, muscle weakness, or unintended weight change. On examination: vitamin D level 14 ng/mL, BP 114/74 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 95 kg. General physical examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat vitamin D level.

Visit note | 2025-11-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Fahim Pramanik, 70, male. Mr. Pramanik complains of trouble falling asleep most nights, waking up tired, and constant worry about his sleep. He reports these issues began after a newborn arrived in the family in Bogura. He works as a homemaker, lives with his spouse, and has Essential hypertension. He denies any depressive symptoms, chest discomfort, or morning headaches. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 18, BP 142/89 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 66 kg. He is alert with normal orientation and anxious affect. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-11-09 03:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Monir Kabir, 46, male. Mr. Kabir presents with a runny nose and symptoms that get worse around dust. He notes his condition has been worse since keeping a cat at home in Badda. He works as a construction worker, lives with family, and has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any fever, earache, or breathing difficulty. On examination: about 12 sneezing fits a day, BP 111/74 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 77 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy with clear secretions. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. Tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-11-09 04:30 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Rehana Sultana, 50, female. Mrs. Sultana reports constant tiredness and brittle nails. She mentions her fatigue worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Bashundhara. She works as a cricket coach, lives alone, and has no comorbidity. She denies any shortness of breath at rest or dizziness. On examination: haemoglobin 10.0 g/dL, BP 133/77 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 73 kg. She shows a craving to chew ice and a sore smooth tongue with little tiredness, along with pale nail beds. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-11-09 04:30 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Zakia Uddin, 77, female. Mrs. Uddin complains that her eye symptoms are worse in air conditioning and after long hours of screen time. She states her discomfort grew worse since moving to a new air-conditioned office in Savar. She works as a madrasa teacher, lives with her family, and has no comorbidity. She denies any eye pain, discharge, or sudden vision loss. On examination: tear break-up time 5 seconds, BP 131/77 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 62 kg. Corneas are clear with reduced tear film stability. Assessment: Dry eye syndrome. Plan: no new medicine was prescribed. She was advised to look away from the screen every 20 minutes, blink often, and use a humidifier. Follow-up in 1 month.
